papers.title: The impact of behavioural activity on the EEG power spectrum, its source localisation, and global functional connectivity in rats Behavioural modulation of rat EEG dynamics.
papers.summary: Analyzed multichannel EEG in freely moving rats (n=116) to assess behavioural activity effects on power spectrum, source localization, and global functional connectivity. Behavioural activity increased 6-8 Hz (peaking at 7 Hz) and gamma/high-gamma power, decreased delta and beta power, and altered connectivity in thalamus; alpha band was unaffected.

papers.title: EEG-based mental workload recognition during multi-tasking scenarios: the role of resting-state normalization and brain region of EEG features.
papers.summary: This study evaluated EEG-based mental workload recognition during multi-tasking using resting-state normalization and regional feature analysis. It achieved up to 93.78% accuracy with a whole-brain model and showed that parietal configurations retained substantial recognition capability with fewer electrodes, with SHAP identifying frontal and parietal contributions.

papers.title: Within-cohort discrimination and cross-cohort transfer of EEG-based ADHD classifiers: An exploratory two-cohort evaluation
papers.summary: This exploratory two-cohort reanalysis tested within-cohort discrimination and cross-cohort transfer of EEG-based ADHD classifiers. Adult spectral classifiers achieved high balanced accuracy (0.95) but cross-cohort spectral balanced accuracy dropped to 0.36-0.47, with reverse cross-cohort ranking, indicating strong internal discrimination did not generalize across cohorts.

papers.title: Neuronal ensembles in visual cortex reactivate during hypnagogic sleep onset
papers.summary: Imaged neuronal ensembles in rodent visual cortex during wake and sleep onset after repeated visual stimulation. Found that NREM1 sleep is the primary sleep-onset state, and neuronal ensembles activated by visual stimuli or locomotion showed increased activity during NREM1, suggesting reactivation underlying hypnagogic hallucinations.

papers.title: Tsmd-net: two-stage multi-domain distillation network for cross-subject MI-EEG domain generalization.
papers.summary: TSMD-Net is a two-stage multi-domain distillation network for cross-subject motor imagery EEG domain generalization, distilling knowledge from multiple domain-specific heads into a unified leader head with feature covariance alignment and hyperbolic supervised contrastive learning. It achieved mean accuracies of 70.21%, 77.82%, and 79.53% on BCI Competition IV 2a, 2b, and the High Gamma Dataset, respectively.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnea severity associates with reduced phase-lag index functional connectivity during N2 sleep.
papers.summary: Retrospectively analyzed polysomnography and 6-channel EEG in 50 patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) or primary snoring to assess associations between OSA severity and spectral power or phase-lag index (PLI) functional connectivity. Found that AHI negatively correlated with delta-band PLI (r=-0.335) and theta-band PLI (r=-0.326) during N2 sleep only, while conventional spectral measures showed no significant correlations.

papers.title: A spatial-channel reconstruction guided frequency-time-space deep neural framework for SSVEP-based brain-computer interface EEG decoding.
papers.summary: SCR-FTSDNN is a spatial-channel reconstruction guided frequency-time-space deep neural network for SSVEP-based BCI EEG decoding, using Fourier transform, temporal convolution, spatial and channel reconstruction convolution modules, and dilated convolution. On the Benchmark and BETA datasets, it achieved superior recognition accuracy and robustness, particularly under limited calibration data.

papers.title: Hyperexcitable but seizure-free: hippocampal network dysfunction in a Wolfram syndrome model
papers.summary: Characterized hippocampal function in a mouse model of Wolfram syndrome carrying a patient orthologous Wfs1 variant. Mutants showed loss of excitatory synapses, hyperexcitable dissociated neurons but no increase in network bursting, no seizures, and a male-specific reduction in hippocampal low-gamma power during intracranial EEG.

papers.title: REM sleep EEG slowing signals basal forebrain integrity in older adults with subjective and mild cognitive impairment
papers.summary: This study examined the relationship between REM sleep EEG slowing and basal forebrain (nucleus basalis of Meynert) volume in older adults with subjective and mild cognitive impairment. Greater REM EEG slowing was associated with smaller NbM volume, and smaller NbM volume was linked to longer sleep latency and poorer episodic memory.

papers.title: Prefrontal EEG Delta-Beta Coupling Marks Depressed State in Adult Siblings
papers.summary: This study analyzed resting-state EEG delta-beta phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) in sibling cohorts to distinguish state versus trait markers of major depressive disorder. Delta-beta-high PAC was elevated over the left-medial frontal region in current MDD but not in remitted MDD or unaffected siblings, indicating it reflects depressive state rather than familial vulnerability.

papers.title: Altered neural prioritization of auditory information during cross-modal attention in children with ADHD.
papers.summary: Examined neural prioritization of auditory information during cross-modal attention in 95 children (46 ADHD, 49 typically developing) using EEG and a visuocued auditory spatial attention task. Children with ADHD showed reduced target lateralization, smaller N2ac, weaker target decoding, and enhanced nontarget decoding, with these neural alterations linked to response-time variability and hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms.

papers.title: 40 Hz Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation Enhances Verbal Free Recall in Healthy Adults by Modulating Frontal Theta Oscillations.
papers.summary: In a randomized, single-blind, sham-controlled three-arm study of 44 healthy young adults, 40 Hz transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation improved verbal free recall compared with sham and 20 Hz stimulation, and increased resting-state frontal theta power transiently; frontal theta changes positively correlated with recall performance and Bayesian mediation supported a theta-dependent model.

papers.title: Machine learning-based source-level EEG functional network biomarkers of antidepressant treatment response in major depressive disorder.
papers.summary: Using baseline resting-state EEG and graph-theory functional networks from 47 MDD patients and 41 healthy controls, this study found that antidepressant non-responders had lower global strength and clustering coefficient and higher path length in high beta, and a support vector machine using nodal features classified 12-week responders vs non-responders with 82.98% accuracy, 85.19% sensitivity, and 80.00% specificity.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Association between Neurovascular Network Dysfunction and Poor Sleep Quality in Patients with Cerebral Small Vessel Disease.
papers.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of 102 patients with cerebral small vessel disease, poor sleep quality (PSQI >5) showed nominal associations with autonomic, cerebral haemodynamic, and resting-state EEG neurovascular network variables, but none survived FDR correction; a multidomain model had an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.758.

papers.title: Hemispheric segregation is evident in early perception, not just higher cognition.
papers.summary: Analyzing an open EEG dataset across language, face, and emotional face tasks, this study found that early N1/N170 lateralization patterns consistent with Gerrits' segregation bias model were most frequent but highly variable, with hemispheric crowding common, indicating that functional hemispheric segregation is detectable during early perception and modulated by handedness and sex.

papers.title: Waveform sharpness identifies the morphological phenotype of high-frequency oscillation-associated spikes in pediatric focal epilepsy.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: In 993 interictal spikes from 20 children with focal epilepsy, mixed-effects and GEE models showed that waveform sharpness was the strongest independent morphological correlate of scalp high-frequency oscillation-associated spikes (adjusted odds ratio 7.41 per 1-SD increase in mixed-effects model), whereas peak-to-peak amplitude, slow-wave area, and duration were not robust independent markers.

papers.title: Neural state reduction: a quantum-inspired framework for how latent conscious thought becomes reportable.
papers.summary: This paper develops a quantum-inspired computational framework for modeling how latent conscious thought becomes reportable, using state vectors, density matrices, and projection operators to represent pre-report neural-cognitive states and introspective measurement. Illustrative simulations show that non-commuting introspective questions produce order effects, selective reporting reduces candidate-state entropy, and overlapping thoughts yield interference-like probability structures, generating testable predictions for EEG/MEG/fMRI and perturbation studies.

papers.title: A Systematic Review of the Maturation of Selected Cortical Auditory Event-Related Potentials in Passive Paradigms: Developmental Changes from Infancy to Early Adulthood.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesized 62 studies to chart developmental trajectories of four cortical auditory event-related potential components (N100, MMN/MMR, P3a, N400) in passive paradigms from infancy to early adulthood. Latency decreased with age across all components, while amplitude trajectories varied by component, and scalp topographies shifted toward increased focal activation with age, providing a normative foundation for typical auditory and language development.

papers.title: Electroencephalography for Radiation-Free Orientation Estimation of Directional Deep Brain Stimulation Leads
papers.summary: Developed and evaluated a radiation-free EEG framework for estimating the rotational orientation of directional deep brain stimulation leads, using a realistic head phantom and postoperative human recordings. In the phantom, a tri-montage approach reduced maximal mean orientation error to 0.59°, and in a patient with bilateral globus pallidus leads, EEG-derived orientations differed from imaging references by about 8° and 15°, remaining stable after downsampling and montage reduction.

papers.title: Brain network differences in second language learning depend on individual competencies.
papers.summary: Eighty-three adults learned Finnish nouns over 14 days using a mobile app with varied learning strategies, and EEG was recorded during a translation recognition task to measure N400 effects. Vocabulary accuracy increased substantially (0.41% to 75.5%) and N400 incongruity effects increased, with high performers showing larger N400 responses; ERP template-map analyses revealed qualitative reorganization of semantic processing, and no single learning strategy provided consistent advantages.

papers.title: Are you afraid? Neurophysiological responses to multidimensional fear in an interactive semi-immersive environment.
papers.summary: This exploratory study used concurrent EEG, heart rate variability, and electrodermal activity to examine brain-body responses to four multidimensional fear scenarios in an interactive semi-immersive environment with ten participants. Results revealed shared neural and autonomic fear markers, including frontal and parietal activation and increased heart rate and skin conductance, along with context-dependent modulation and a weak but significant global EEG-autonomic association.

papers.title: MRI-guided personalized tDCS planning for target engagement of the swallowing motor cortex after stroke: a finite-element modeling study.
papers.summary: This finite-element modeling study compared electric field strength and focality across three tDCS montages targeting the swallowing motor cortex in 50 poststroke dysphagia patients using MRI-based head models. The optimized circular montage (Opt-C) produced the highest electric field strength and target-specific focality, and small circular electrodes outperformed square electrodes, supporting image-guided personalized tDCS planning for precision neuromodulation.

papers.title: Neurophysiological affective reactivity classification and its stability in individuals with cannabis use disorder.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology
papers.summary: This study replicated and extended neuroaffective reactivity profiles in 44 individuals with cannabis use disorder using late positive potential (LPP) during a probabilistic choice task and affective picture viewing. At two lab visits one week apart, k-means clustering consistently identified two groups based on cannabis versus pleasant LPP amplitudes, but clusters did not differ in choice behavior or problematic use indicators, and individual-level retest reliability was low.

papers.title: Neurological prognostication after cardiac arrest: evidence review and institutional protocol proposal.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on neurological prognostication after cardiac arrest, highlighting reliable predictors of poor outcome such as absent brainstem reflexes at 72 hours, persistent EEG suppression, bilateral absence of cortical N20 potentials, and diffuse MRI abnormalities. It proposes an institutional protocol for Hospital de Clínicas de Porto Alegre that organizes assessments from ICU admission through day 5 after return of spontaneous circulation.

papers.title: Highly stretchable, hair-compatible multichannel neural interface with time-stable hydrogel for high-fidelity long-term EEG sensing.
papers.summary: This paper presents MindStretcH, a stretchable and hair-compatible EEG platform integrating a kirigami-patterned elastomeric mesh, deformable EGaIn interconnects, and detachable hydrogel-based conical electrodes. The system maintained stable electrode-scalp contact and consistent task-related EEG activity in longitudinal motor-imagery and repeated online BCI experiments without measurable deterioration.

papers.title: Blunted Neural Error Monitoring Amplifies the Adverse Effect of Childhood Maltreatment on Depressive Symptoms: Time-Domain and Time-Frequency Analysis.
papers.summary: Examined whether neurophysiological and behavioral indicators of performance monitoring interact with childhood maltreatment to predict depressive symptoms in 192 Chinese university students during an Eriksen Flanker task with EEG. Blunted error-related negativity and error-related delta amplified the adverse effect of childhood maltreatment, especially emotional neglect, on depressive symptoms, whereas error-related theta and posterror accuracy did not show such interactions.

papers.title: Machine Learning Models for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection: Systematic Review With a Pediatric and Engineering Perspective.
papers.summary: Systematically reviewed machine learning and deep learning approaches for early autism spectrum disorder detection, covering data modalities such as questionnaires, home video, speech, eye tracking, EEG/MEG, MRI/fMRI, wearables, and multimodal data. Reported diagnostic performance varied substantially across populations and validation settings, with external validation, data leakage, explainability, fairness, and workflow integration identified as major barriers to clinical translation.

papers.title: Electroencephalography research in neuropathic pain (Review).
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes EEG and mechanistic evidence in neuropathic pain, reporting relatively recurrent resting-state theta increases and dominant-frequency slowing as candidate biomarkers. It highlights heterogeneity in alpha, beta, and gamma findings and aberrant prefrontal-limbic and sensorimotor connectivity, while noting that computational methods, graph theory, and machine learning are advancing objective individualized pain assessment.

papers.title: Simulation-Based Neurodiagnostic Team Training for Critically Ill Patients with External Ventricular Drains: Design, Implementation, and Outcomes.
papers.summary: This study designed, implemented, and evaluated a high-fidelity simulation-based curriculum for neurodiagnostic technologists performing continuous EEG setup in critically ill patients with external ventricular drains. Participants reported increased confidence, better workflow understanding, and improved communication with nursing teams, supporting simulation as a tool for enhancing safety and team performance in EVD-dependent cEEG monitoring.

papers.title: Familial prrt2-negative paroxysmal kinesigenic dyskinesia mimicking frontal lobe epilepsy: a video-eeg/polygraphic documentation.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: No abstract provided.

papers.title: Decoding Dietary Fat: Molecular Sensing, Brain Integration, and the Biology of Flavor.
papers.journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on dietary fat perception, describing CD36 and GPR120 as principal lipid sensors alongside FFAR1, GPR84, FFAR2, and TGR5, and integrating oral detection with retronasal olfaction, trigeminal signaling, endocrine responses, and cortical reward networks. It concludes that fat perception is a distributed, adaptive, and metabolically regulated system rather than an isolated sensory pathway, and calls for methodological standardization to advance personalized dietary interventions.

papers.title: Spinal Mechanisms of Testosterone Involved in Itch Regulation.
papers.summary: Testosterone suppresses acute and chronic itch in mice via spinal androgen receptors on PAX2+ GABAergic interneurons, enhancing GABA release and inhibiting GRPR+ neurons through GABAAR. Orchiectomy increased itch sensitivity that was reversed by testosterone, and the antipruritic effect was blocked by intrathecal flutamide or bicuculline.

papers.title: IgG4 sensitizes human dorsal root ganglia neurons and patient-derived IgG induces FcγR-dependent pain hypersensitivity in mice
papers.summary: The study shows that IgG4 from chronic pain patients sensitizes human dorsal root ganglia neurons and induces FcγR-dependent pain hypersensitivity in mice, with IgG4 colocalizing with B-cell signatures in patient DRGs and FcγR1A/CD64 expressed on small sensory neurons. Recombinant IgG4 increased neuronal excitability, and patient-derived IgG produced mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity in B-cell-deficient mice but not in FcγR-deficient mice.

papers.title: Genes Do Not Read DSM: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex May Dominate with Multi-Neuropsychiatric Symptoms.
papers.summary: The case describes a 26-year-old woman with panic-like episodes initially diagnosed as primary panic disorder, later found to have focal seizures from the left frontotemporal region associated with tuberous sclerosis complex. Treatment with lacosamide eliminated epileptiform activity and substantially reduced panic-like episodes and depressive/anxiety symptoms.

papers.title: Late-onset atypical pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1A with intracranial calcification and epilepsy associated with a novel GNAS variant: a case report.
papers.summary: The case reports a 59-year-old woman with late-onset atypical pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1A, presenting with cognitive decline, seizures, and intracranial calcification, and a novel GNAS variant (c.285C>G: p.Ser95Arg). Treatment with calcium, calcitriol, and levetiracetam resolved seizures and normalized serum calcium, but cognitive improvement was limited.

papers.title: Neonatal rotavirus encephalopathy with white matter injury: A case report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 35-week preterm neonate with rotavirus-associated encephalopathy presenting with lethargy and hypotonia, diagnosed via positive stool PCR. Brain MRI showed bilateral periventricular and deep white matter diffusion restriction, highlighting the need for rotavirus testing in unexplained neonatal encephalopathy even without gastrointestinal symptoms.

papers.title: Deep-Learning-Assisted Single-Shot Plasma Emission Imaging for Pollen Morphology Reconstruction and Apparent Hydration-State Classification.
papers.summary: The paper combines single-shot plasma emission imaging with deep learning to reconstruct pollen morphology and classify hydration states, achieving approximately 76% leave-one-out accuracy using chromaticity features and a support vector machine. The results suggest that plasma emission contains structural and hydration-associated information for rapid pollen phenotyping.

papers.title: Cortical Spreading Depression Mimicking Ischemic Stroke: A Case Report of Complex Hemiplegic Migraine with Reversible Cortical Magnetic Resonance Imaging Changes.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 66-year-old man with hemiplegic migraine presenting with acute stroke-like symptoms, where MRI showed diffusion-weighted hyperintensities without ADC restriction, indicating transient cytotoxic edema rather than infarction. The findings emphasize that integrating clinical context with MRI, particularly absence of ADC restriction, can differentiate hemiplegic migraine from ischemic stroke.

papers.title: Anti-KLHL11 antibody encephalitis without detectable malignancy: a case report and literature review.
papers.summary: The paper reports a 62-year-old male with anti-KLHL11 antibody encephalitis without detectable malignancy who presented with recurrent generalized tonic-clonic seizures, and it systematically reviews 13 published cases. Among reviewed cases, ataxia, dysarthria, and gaze palsy/nystagmus were common; after immunotherapy 6 improved, 3 remained stable, and 4 deteriorated, with 2 deaths from central respiratory failure.

papers.title: NeuroDance: study protocol for a non-randomized multicenter study of a mixed-style dance intervention for people with Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: This study protocol outlines NeuroDance, a multicenter non-randomized trial across four European countries to evaluate a mixed-style dance intervention for Parkinson's disease. The intervention combines multiple dance styles with rhythmic auditory cueing and improvisation, with primary outcomes including gait, mobility, balance, cognition, and quality of life, and secondary outcomes exploring neurophysiological adaptations.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
